To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
parenting styles and parental physical abuse might be responsible for setting the path to overweight/obesity.

(i) female adolescents who have experienced severe parental physical and medium/high parental emotional warmth in childhood are at risk for becoming overweight/obese, (ii) male adolescents who experienced low or medium parenting monitoring in childhood are at heightened risk for becoming overweight, and this effect is stronger in male adolescents who come from a family that receives welfare.

(1) female students who experienced parental physical abuse in childhood and who also perceive their parents as being warm are more likely to be overweight or obese; (2) for male students, the likelihood of being overweight or obese is higher when parents show low levels of parental monitoring; and (3), in the context of male students, the risk of overweight/ obesity increases when parents show low monitoring in conjunction with receiving welfare.
In summary, our research is concerned with
parenting styles and parental physical abuse as possible risk factors for the development of overweight/obese adolescents.
